title: Why browser pages needed behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain why browser pages needed behaviour and describe JavaScript's role in web development.

understand.concept: Early web pages were primarily documents that linked to other documents. As pages became interactive, developers needed a way to respond to user actions, update content, validate input, and communicate with browser capabilities. JavaScript became a major language for adding this behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding why scripting exists explains the role JavaScript plays alongside HTML structure and CSS presentation. It also helps separate browser behaviour from server processing.
understand.analogy: HTML provides the document, CSS controls presentation, and JavaScript adds behaviour when a user interacts with the page.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; language standards and host runtime APIs have precise technical boundaries.

explain.narrative: The button listens for a click and JavaScript updates the text. The page responds without requiring a full document navigation.

examples.explanation: The button listens for a click and JavaScript updates the text. The page responds without requiring a full document navigation.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser page displays or updates text using JavaScript.

questions.prompt: What role does JavaScript commonly add to a web page?
questions.explanation: JavaScript responds to events and can update page behaviour and content.

questions.prompt: What should you identify before using a JavaScript API?
